[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "midivolt"
version = "0.1.0rc1"
description = "Modular, commercially oriented MIDI creation and arrangement engine"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"]
dependencies = [
  "pretty_midi>=0.2.11,<0.3",
  "mido>=1.3,<2",
  "music21>=9.1,<10",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
audio = ["basic-pitch==0.4.0", "numpy>=1.23.5,<2", "scipy>=1.10,<2"]
dev = ["pytest>=8,<10", "numpy>=1.23.5,<2", "scipy>=1.10,<2"]
hub = ["huggingface_hub>=0.27,<2"]

[project.scripts]
midivolt = "midivolt.cli:main"
midivolt-prompt = "midivolt.prompt_cli:main"
midivolt-ai = "midivolt.ai_cli:main"
midivolt-bridge = "midivolt.bridge_cli:main"
midivolt-tsov = "midivolt.tsov_cli:main"
midivolt-review = "midivolt.review_cli:main"
midivolt-model = "midivolt.model_cli:main"
midivolt-hub = "midivolt.model_hub_cli:main"
midivolt-env = "midivolt.environment_cli:main"
midivolt-accept = "midivolt.acceptance_cli:main"
midivolt-cubase = "midivolt.cubase_cli:main"
midivolt-transcribe = "midivolt.transcribe:main"
midivolt-evaluate = "midivolt.evaluate:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

# MIDIVOLT

**AI-ready MIDI composition and arrangement engine.** This is a Python CLI developer release candidate with external AI model runner adapters. No pretrained weights, GUI DAW or VST3 plug-in are bundled.

## What works in this first slice

- Read and write Standard MIDI Files with **pretty_midi** (MIT).
- Interpret lead-sheet chord symbols with **music21** (BSD-3-Clause).
- Generate separate chord and bass MIDI tracks without changing the original tracks.
- Detect a rough musical key and inspect a MIDI arrangement.
- Optionally transcribe audio to MIDI using **Spotify Basic Pitch** (Apache-2.0).
- A typed generator-provider contract for future models; **no model weights or pretrained systems are silently downloaded**.
- Windows and Linux core CI. No VST3/AU/AAX binaries yet.

## Windows developer RC 0.1.0rc1

The **single integration branch** `integration/windows-rc1-20261020` consolidates
previous Draft PRs #1–#7 without merging to `main`. Its Windows workflow builds
an installable Python wheel and a ZIP with installer, smoke test, licensing
notices and SHA256 checksum. It does not redistribute dependencies or Python.

After downloading and verifying the artifact from the
[Windows Developer RC workflow](https://github.com/kevin781130-netizen/MIDIVOLT/actions/workflows/windows-rc.yml),
extract the ZIP and run on Windows with your trusted Python 3.11 installation:

```powershell
# Explicit network consent to fetch Python dependencies:
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Install-MIDIVOLT.ps1 -AllowNetwork

# Or no network downloads if you supplied a complete, trusted local wheelhouse:
powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Install-MIDIVOLT.ps1 -Wheelhouse "D:\audited-wheels"
```

The installer refuses existing destinations and runs local MIDI generation,
locked-track review, Cubase Type 1 export and Model Hub catalog smoke checks.
See [Windows RC packaging and limitations](docs/windows-rc.md).
The developer RC is **CLI-only**, and real Cubase GUI/model GPU acceptance is
not claimed by the workflow.

## Real opt-in AI MIDI generation (Cut31 experimental)

After installing this branch, midivolt-ai now accepts a real OpenAI API key or a separately installed local Ollama model. It sends an explicitly authorized prompt, rejects malformed or out-of-range AI note events, and writes separate editable MIDI tracks. No model checkpoints or API keys are bundled. Local mocked-server tests do NOT prove musical quality or actual paid-provider availability.

```powershell
$env:MIDIVOLT_OPENAI_API_KEY = 'YOUR_OWN_API_KEY'
midivolt-ai --provider openai --model YOUR_SUPPORTED_MODEL --prompt '8 bars of chords, melody, bass and drums in D minor' --out new-ai.mid --allow-network
midivolt-ai --provider ollama --model YOUR_INSTALLED_LOCAL_MODEL --prompt '4 bars of melody in A minor' --out local-ai.mid --allow-network
```

To extend existing MIDI, add --input source.mid --manifest proposal.json and use midivolt-review preview/apply --approve before final publish. Source tracks are hash-protected and left unchanged. See [Cut31 provider guide](docs/product/MIDI_AGENT_CUT31_AI_PROVIDER.md). No VST3/AU/AAX or stand-alone GUI yet.

## Text prompt to editable multitrack MIDI (Cut30 product prototype)

An **original, deterministic rules engine** now generates independently
editable Chords, Melody, Bass and General MIDI Drums tracks from bounded
English or Chinese musical instructions. It can extend an existing
constant-tempo 4/4 Standard MIDI without editing the source. This
command **does not use an LLM**; the provider-based AI generator and
VST/standalone GUI remain separate work.

```sh
midivolt-prompt --prompt "Full song, 8 bars in D minor at 110 bpm" --out new-sketch.mid
midivolt-prompt --prompt "請寫8小節 F#小調 旋律 貝斯 100 BPM" --out melody-bass.mid
midivolt-prompt --input original.mid --prompt "Extend with 4 bars of sparse melody" --out extended.mid
```

See [MIDI Agent feature-parity status, what is missing and Cut30
scope](docs/product/MIDI_AGENT_PARITY_CUT30.md). No third-party product
source/UI/assets were copied. The separate top-level drum research branch
is **not** the packaging/product branch and cannot be blindly merged.

## Install

Python **3.11** is used to intersect the supported versions of music21 9.x and the optional Basic Pitch 0.4.0. Use a virtual environment:

```powershell
py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
```

Linux/macOS: `python3.11 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e ".[dev]"`.

Optional audio module (heavier dependencies, not part of CI):

```powershell
python -m pip install -e ".[audio]"
```

## External workstations: Sawdust and tsov

MIDIVOLT can now create target-specific **standard MIDI** files for separately installed [Sawdust](https://github.com/NeonMedusa/Sawdust) (MIT) and [tsov](https://github.com/luolianst/tsov) (AGPL-3.0):

```shell
midivolt-bridge --target sawdust --input demo.mid --out demo-sawdust.mid
midivolt-bridge --target sawdust --input demo.mid --out demo-grid.mid --quantize
midivolt-bridge --target tsov --input demo.mid --out demo-tsov.mid
```

Import the resulting MIDI in the target application's UI. `--quantize` is optional and lossy; original input files are never overwritten. The command prints a JSON compatibility report with known track, timing, and automation limitations. See [bridge documentation](docs/sawdust-tsov-bridge.md). The other applications and their native project formats are **not** bundled.

## AI editing in an external tsov Agent via MCP (experimental)

The original Apache-2.0 MIDIVOLT client can talk to a **separately installed** AGPL-3.0 tsov project through a child process. No tsov source, model weights or Python 3.12 dependency is shipped by MIDIVOLT. tsov's natural-language `edit_score` tool runs in its own environment and uses the LLM endpoint configured in tsov.

```powershell
midivolt-tsov --python "C:\\tsov\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" --root "C:\\tsov" projects
midivolt-tsov --python "C:\\tsov\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" --root "C:\\tsov" status --project demo
midivolt-tsov --python "C:\\tsov\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" --root "C:\\tsov" edit --project demo --track 0 --feedback "Preserve the motif, add a short variation" --apply
midivolt-tsov --python "C:\\tsov\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" --root "C:\\tsov" undo --project demo --apply
```

Default: read-only. Changes require `--apply`. tsov returns the **after-apply diff**; it is not a pre-approval preview. See [tsov MCP setup, protections and licensing](docs/tsov-mcp.md). Run `pytest -q tests/test_tsov_mcp.py` for protocol tests with a simulated server. Live Windows acceptance remains unverified.

## Reviewable AI arrangement candidates

**MIDIVOLT now supports a review-first multi-track arrangement workflow.** AI models or external workstations can generate a candidate MIDI; the built-in engine validates melody locks, checks changed notes and only exports an approved copy. This is a validation/editing workflow, **not yet a trained text-to-MIDI model**.

```powershell
# Work with an AI-generated MIDI candidate
midivolt-review propose --input melody.mid --candidate candidate.mid --manifest proposal.json --lock 0
midivolt-review preview --manifest proposal.json
midivolt-review apply --manifest proposal.json --out approved.mid --approve

# Or propose chords/bass from built-in deterministic arranger
midivolt-review propose --input melody.mid --chords "Fmaj7 Dm7 Gm7 C7" --candidate-out generated.mid --manifest generated.json --lock 0
```

Source and candidate hashes are checked before apply. Locked tracks preserve notes, expression and identity; tempo, meter and key maps cannot silently change. Existing output files will not be overwritten. [Review engine contract and limits](docs/arrangement-review.md).

## Optional local pretrained model generation

Two model runner adapters now call the upstream **Text2midi** Transformer (text-to-MIDI) and **Anticipatory Music Transformer** (melody-conditioned accompaniment) using local model assets in external Python environments. They do **not** download weights or install external model repositories:

```powershell
midivolt-model text2midi --python MODEL_PYTHON --checkout TEXT2MIDI_CHECKOUT --checkpoint MODEL_FILE --vocab REMI_PICKLE --t5-dir LOCAL_T5_DIR --prompt "F major romantic synth flute" --source melody.mid --out candidate.mid --manifest plan.json --lock 0
midivolt-model anticipation --python MODEL_PYTHON --checkout ANTICIPATION_CHECKOUT --checkpoint MODEL_DIR --source melody.mid --melody-program 73 --seconds 12 --out candidate.mid --manifest plan.json --lock 0
midivolt-review preview --manifest plan.json
midivolt-review apply --manifest plan.json --out approved.mid --approve
```

Each command requires real existing local paths. Choose one model command per candidate (do not reuse output names). The generated MIDI is appended to a copy of the original source, then passed to the existing locked-track review engine. No production model inference, Windows/Cubase, or VST3 acceptance has been verified yet. Read the [model installation, security and licensing guide](docs/model-adapters.md).

## Model Hub (catalog and controlled downloads)

`midivolt-hub` is an opt-in Hugging Face catalog and model asset manager.
Local operations require no internet; `--online` explicitly enables
remote search/model-metadata inspection. `download` requires a pinned
40-character revision, explicit license acceptance, explicit download consent,
and a second acknowledgment for unsafe BIN/PKL asset formats.

```powershell
pip install -e ".[hub,dev]"
midivolt-hub catalog
midivolt-hub inspect text2midi --online
midivolt-hub inspect anticipation --online
midivolt-hub doctor anticipation --python "C:\\models\\anticipation\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe" --checkout "C:\\models\\anticipation" --checkpoint "C:\\MIDIVOLT\\Models\\anticipation"
```

See [Model Hub guide](docs/model-hub.md). This is **not** a one-click
model installer: upstream Python environments and tokenizer/model
dependencies still need to be provisioned separately.

## Model-specific Python runtime environments and actual inference acceptance

MIDIVOLT can now create a **separate version-pinned venv** for Text2midi and
Anticipatory. Commands `midivolt-env plan`, `create --confirm-create`,
`install --confirm-install` and `verify` check the upstream source Git SHA,
the `requirements.txt` SHA256, local Python version and installed packages.
Online pip installation requires an additional `--allow-network`, while the
`--wheelhouse` option supports offline dependency provisioning.

`midivolt-accept` performs a **real model inference** only after the user's
`--confirm-inference`, validates the generated candidate MIDI and melody lock,
and writes an acceptance JSON with elapsed time and hashes. No weights,
tokenizers or Python interpreter are fetched automatically.

```powershell
# Approved upstream checkout and existing Python 3.10 installation required
midivolt-env plan text2midi --checkout SOURCE --revision APPROVED40CHARSHA --base-python PYTHON310 --env NEW_VENV
midivolt-env create text2midi --checkout SOURCE --revision APPROVED40CHARSHA --base-python PYTHON310 --env NEW_VENV --confirm-create
midivolt-env install --env NEW_VENV --allow-network --confirm-install
midivolt-env verify --env NEW_VENV
# Real checkpoint acceptance: see the complete command in docs/model-runtime.md
```

See [Windows setup and actual model inference acceptance](docs/model-runtime.md).
No GPU, end-to-end model quality or Cubase compatibility is asserted by unit tests.

## Cubase SMF Type 1 export and acceptance profile

MIDIVOLT now has a strict **MIDI event-preservation gate** for Cubase:
`midivolt-cubase check`, `prepare` and `compare`.
A Type 1 export with a conductor track and explicit 480 PPQ is created
without editing the source MIDI. This includes tempo/meter, channels, notes,
CC, pitch bend, SysEx and markers. The exporter aborts if MIDI event content
changes or a positive-duration note is collapsed by PPQ scaling.

```powershell
midivolt-cubase check --input approved.mid
midivolt-cubase prepare --input approved.mid --out cubase-import.mid --ppq 480
# After a real Cubase import + export:
midivolt-cubase compare --reference cubase-import.mid --returned cubase-roundtrip.mid --strict
```

See [Cubase import instructions and strict MIDI event checks](docs/cubase-acceptance.md).
Automated tests cannot verify Cubase GUI/VST3 playback; that remains an
explicit Windows real-application acceptance test.

## Quick start

```shell
midivolt create --chords "Fmaj7 Dm7 Gm7 C7" --bpm 70 --out demo.mid
midivolt analyze --input demo.mid
midivolt arrange --input melody.mid --chords "Fmaj7 Dm7 Gm7 C7" --out arranged.mid
midivolt transcribe --input solo.wav --out solo.mid
```

The `arrange` operation deep-copies the MIDI data, retains every existing track and note, and adds separate named `MIDIVOLT Chords` and `MIDIVOLT Bass` tracks. MIDI tick/tempo mapping is used, so existing tempo maps are preserved. Chords are one bar each in **4/4 quarter-note units** by default; this is not yet a meter-aware arranger. Set `--beats-per-chord` to override.

Existing output files are protected: use `--overwrite` to replace them. Input and output may not be the same file unless explicitly overwritten.

## Current limitations / next modules

- Text2midi and Anticipatory model runners are connected to upstream inference functions **only in separately provisioned environments**. Real trained checkpoint quality, GPU execution and commercial rights remain to be validated.
- MIDI file interchange with independently installed DAWs exists; no embedded DAW/VST3 instrument/effect, live MIDI routing, piano-roll UI, or MusicXML export.
- Key analysis is an estimate, not guaranteed harmonic ground truth.
- Audio-to-MIDI quality depends on source audio; Basic Pitch is best tested with isolated instruments and can fail on dense mixes.
- Chord accompaniment uses a straightforward root-position voicing; sophisticated voice leading and genre-specific arrangement are future milestones.
- MIDI files and generated materials remain local by default. Model Hub **online** search/download and explicitly authorized pip environment setup can contact external services; upstream model/LLM deployments may have their own network behavior.

## Architecture

- `src/midivolt/arrange.py` — non-destructive MIDI accompaniment.
- `src/midivolt/theory.py` — chord parsing / rough key detection.
- `src/midivolt/audio.py` — optional Basic Pitch adapter.
- `src/midivolt/io.py` — validated MIDI file I/O.
- `src/midivolt/providers.py` — pluggable future AI generation contract.
- `src/midivolt/cli.py` — runnable command-line entry point.

## Licensing

MIDIVOLT is Apache-2.0. Third-party packages are installed as dependencies rather than vendored. See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for direct dependencies and licensing boundaries. Review model **weights**, data and redistribution conditions independently before adding models.

## Experimental isolated-stem WAV → MIDI baseline

The consolidated developer main now includes the independent `feat/benchmark-foundation` work under the standard `src/midivolt/` package layout, **not** a second top-level `midivolt` package. Pitched stems can run through optional Spotify Basic Pitch, and an opt-in DSP baseline maps kick/snare/closed-hat on isolated drum stems. It outputs separate MIDI tracks plus a multitrack SMF, without asserting precise transcription accuracy or automatic instrument separation.

Use Python 3.11 and explicitly install optional dependencies: `python -m pip install -e ".[audio,dev]"`. Run `midivolt-transcribe --input stems --output midi --tempo 138 --drum-engine dsp` (omit `--drum-engine dsp` to skip drums); evaluate aligned predictions with `midivolt-evaluate --reference REF.mid --predicted OUT.mid`. See [transcription details](docs/transcription/BASIC_PITCH.md) and [benchmark plan](docs/benchmark/PLAN.md).

The benchmark dataset commercial gate stays **fail-closed** until external rights/evidence are approved. This is a developer baseline, not a qualified commercial transcription engine; real WAV/Cubase/Windows acceptance is pending. Original project and source WAVs are not silently overwritten.

# Third-party software and rights register

MIDIVOLT installs packages through Python packaging; their source code or trained weights are not copied into this repository.

| Project | Role | Upstream license | Link |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pretty_midi | MIDI data handling | MIT | https://github.com/craffel/pretty-midi |
| music21 | Chord parsing / harmonic analysis | BSD-3-Clause | https://github.com/cuthbertLab/music21 |
| Spotify Basic Pitch (optional) | Audio-to-MIDI | Apache-2.0 | https://github.com/spotify/basic-pitch |
| Sawdust (standalone; **not included**) | External MIDI import/VST host | MIT | https://github.com/NeonMedusa/Sawdust |
| tsov (standalone; **not included**) | External AI-native DAW | AGPL-3.0 | https://github.com/luolianst/tsov |

The bridge emits standard MIDI files. Neither Sawdust nor tsov is an installed dependency, vendored component, or included executable. Transferring a file to a separately installed application does not itself embed its source code in MIDIVOLT. New linking, redistribution or hosted integrations require separate legal review.

The licenses of optional/transitive dependencies, corpora, sounds, models, checkpoints, training data and bundled plugins must be checked before commercial distribution. Keep full notices in builds.

**Not incorporated/downloaded by this PR:** Text2midi, Anticipatory Music Transformer, MIDI-GPT, MT3, MIDI-LLM and other pretrained models. Source license != checkpoint/training data license.

## tsov MCP boundary (experimental)

The optional client in `src/midivolt/tsov_mcp.py` and `src/midivolt/tsov_cli.py` is MIDIVOLT-owned code implementing MCP JSON-RPC. It launches an independently installed tsov process; no tsov source, checkpoints, assets or dependencies are vendored here. The tsov software retains AGPL-3.0 and may entail additional obligations if modified, combined, hosted or redistributed. Treat the process boundary as an engineering choice rather than a legal exemption; obtain counsel for the final commercial deployment model.

## Text2midi and Anticipatory Music Transformer runners

Optional external upstream source repositories (not copied, vendored or installed): [AMAAI-Lab/Text2midi](https://github.com/AMAAI-Lab/Text2midi) (MIT), [jthickstun/anticipation](https://github.com/jthickstun/anticipation) (Apache-2.0). Hugging Face pretrained model cards currently list Apache-2.0 for both [amaai-lab/text2midi](https://huggingface.co/amaai-lab/text2midi) and [stanford-crfm/music-medium-800k](https://huggingface.co/stanford-crfm/music-medium-800k). No pretrained weights, model code, MIDI datasets, or T5 tokenizer files are bundled. Text2midi vocabulary is a Python pickle; execute only trusted files. Reconfirm model weights, datasets, dependencies, media/music rights, copyright/attribution and commercial distribution obligations before shipping a binary.

## MIDIVOLT Model Hub

The optional Hugging Face client (`huggingface_hub`) is a runtime dependency only when `midivolt-hub ... --online` or `download` is used. No source models, weights, soundfonts or tokenizers are bundled. Users explicitly select an immutable revision, accept the model's advertised license, and authorize each file download. Local trust and separate downstream dataset/weight license review remain necessary. The Model Hub deliberately excludes Text2midi's `soundfont.sf2` pending a separate provenance and license review.
